Shamsa Alnahyan

Shamsa Alnahyan (b. 2004, Dubai) is a curator and art consultant based in Dubai. Her practice sits at the intersection of curiosity, human emotion, and an anthropological attention to the traces, rituals, and behaviours of everyday life.

Alnahyan questions translation: how an idea becomes form, how material carries and transforms meaning, and how histories, both personal and collective, can be reinterpreted through an artistic lens. She is interested in how individuals become vessels for ideas, geographies, beliefs, and inherited narratives, and how these are reshaped through lived experience.

Her work considers the forces shaping the contemporary art landscape, particularly within the UAE, where she was raised. Growing up in an international city has informed her interest in how nationality, time, and cultural exchange shape the experience of belonging within a cosmopolitan society.

Working closely with artists, Alnahyan engages with the processes that shape the art world around her, including the act of making itself. Moving between the positions of an insider and an observer, she remains attentive to the relationships between artistic practice, cultural context, and the creative economy, exploring how these intersect to produce meaningful expressions that resonate with diverse audiences.

شمسة آل نهيان (مواليد 2004، دبي) قيّمة فنية ومستشارة فنية مقيمة في دبي. تقع ممارستها عند تقاطع الفضول والعاطفة الإنسانية والاهتمام الأنثروبولوجي بآثار الحياة اليومية وطقوسها وسلوكياتها.

تتساءل آل نهيان عن الترجمة: كيف تتحوّل الفكرة إلى شكل، وكيف تحمل المادة المعنى وتحوّله، وكيف يمكن إعادة قراءة التواريخ، الشخصية منها والجماعية، من خلال منظور فني. وتهتم بالكيفية التي يصبح بها الأفراد أوعيةً للأفكار والجغرافيات والمعتقدات والسرديات الموروثة، وكيف يُعاد تشكيلها عبر التجربة المعاشة.

يتأمل عملها القوى التي تشكّل المشهد الفني المعاصر، ولا سيما في دولة الإمارات العربية المتحدة حيث نشأت. وقد أسهمت نشأتها في مدينة عالمية في تشكيل اهتمامها بالكيفية التي تصوغ بها الجنسية والزمن والتبادل الثقافي تجربةَ الانتماء داخل مجتمع متعدد الثقافات.

من خلال عملها الوثيق مع الفنانين، تنخرط آل نهيان في العمليات التي تشكّل العالم الفني من حولها، بما في ذلك فعل الصنع ذاته. وبتنقّلها بين موقعَي المطّلعة من الداخل والمراقِبة من الخارج، تبقى منتبهةً للعلاقات بين الممارسة الفنية والسياق الثقافي والاقتصاد الإبداعي، مستكشفةً كيف تتقاطع هذه العناصر لتنتج تعبيرات ذات معنى تلامس جماهير متنوعة.

Curating

Snakes & Ladders

MamarLab, Abu Dhabi — 22–31 January 2026

Snakes and Ladders is an exhibition dedicated to life and its dance between fate and chaos. Here, there are no advantages or guarantees: it is chance, encounter, karma, and arbitrary choice that lead each person through life. Inviting its viewers and artists to question and navigate the realities that arise through opportunities and pitfalls.

This exhibition seeks to explore each artist's experiences in life and how their artworks help frame their setbacks, advances, and realisations in between them. Whether through space, physical and metaphysical, or through storytelling, emotional and spiritual, artists re-contextualize what it means to live their lives through every twist and turn.

One hundred boxes and a pair of dice, the game lures the player to never trust the game itself, but rather the fate that will carry them up the ranks or the misfortune that drops them from their places. Snakes present as moments of failure and setbacks, yet beckon the player to reflect on their position. Ladders present moments of opportunity and positive progression, bringing the player to a higher, more favourable place. Both twist fate, putting the player in a vulnerable position.

Artists: Gigi, Ina Michaelian, Klaithem, Maitha Bushelaibi, Reem Ali, Safeya Sharif, Sarine Semerjian, Yoshi (Aisha Al Ali)

Curators: Shamsa Alnahyan, Nicolò Venelli
